answers.ask: Is something chasing the player from behind, or does the run only end on hitting an obstacle?
answers.answer: The run ends when the player hits an obstacle; no chasing character is needed.

answers.ask: Should the Zootopia influence show as anthropomorphic animal characters and signage, or only as the bright stylized art direction?
answers.answer: Use bright stylized art direction only, with a jungle-temple setting; do not add Zootopia characters or signage.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D endless runner map set in a bright, stylized jungle-temple environment. A forward-running track forms three parallel lanes through dense jungle ruins, with temple stonework, foliage, and obstacles arranged along the route; no chasing character, animal characters, or themed signage.
agent_notes: Stated as an endless runner, so Infinite Runner and its genre-wide P6, which the endless track needs anyway for speed-derived obstacle spacing. Temple Run is the named reference but the prompt overrides its steering with three lanes and a swipe to switch between them, which is the lane-snap fork, so Lane Runner is the preset with its own shape and all three of its options intact. Added hazard-kill because the answer makes contact with an obstacle the thing that ends the run, and obstacle-jump because the Temple Run vocabulary the prompt invokes includes gaps and hurdles as well as lane blockers. Without a user I decided the jungle temple is a themed skin on the chunk queue rather than distinct biome maps, so no P4, and I took the answer's instruction to keep the Zootopia influence to bright stylized art direction with no anthropomorphic characters or signage.
